limitations: One seed, one configuration, 500 optimizer updates, 16.35 million CE targets.
17.08 percent of one epoch; no full corpus pass and no repetition.
Training CE is a single 64-sequence microbatch mean with dropout 0.1 active.
Validation CE uses the full split in eval mode, so train and validation levels are not directly comparable and cannot be used to test overfitting.
The v3.1-L timer lacked explicit GPU synchronization; timings are within about 2 percent by wall-clock arithmetic.
Router telemetry entropy is computed over top-2 assignment counts, not over the softmax distribution; the two differ and are reported separately here.
Specialization inference used 120 validation sequences per model at seq_len 512, on three source-pure validation sets only; the test split was not read.
Source-level routing divergence is a coarse probe; token- or feature-level routing structure was not identified.
No GPU numerical resume parity was tested, and none is claimed.
Theoretical compute is an estimate under documented assumptions, not a hardware counter measurement.

estimate.assumption: 6ND with N = all 98,340,864 parameters, because dense MoE activates every expert for every token; attention score and value matmuls ignored (about 1.5 percent of per-token FLOPs). CE targets, not padded positions, are the token count.

recommendations.expected_information_gain: Decides whether the MoE layout adds anything over a dense MLP at this scale, and whether the aux weight or routing objective needs revision.
recommendations.gpu_work: None for analysis; one short bounded run if a new objective is approved.
recommendations.main_risks: Cheap probes may again be inconclusive; a change of routing objective would alter frozen Architecture A and needs separate authorization.
recommendations.option: B. Investigate expert specialization with bounded probes

recommendations.expected_information_gain: Measures the still-decreasing validation curve and tests stability and resume parity beyond 500 updates.
recommendations.gpu_work: One bounded run, new budget and checkpoint policy required.
recommendations.main_risks: Linear GPU time and disk growth (1.57 GB per state); no new capability at this scale; improvement per update already fell by about 10x.

recommendations.expected_information_gain: Would cut dense-MoE expert FLOPs by E/k = 4x and remove the workaround cost.
recommendations.gpu_work: Environment validation plus a sparse smoke and short run later.
recommendations.main_risks: The fault reproduced on torch 2.14.1+rocm7.2; no stable 2.15/2.16 exists. Any upgrade changes the validated environment and needs the full ladder.
recommendations.option: C. Revisit Sparse-MoE after a stable PyTorch/ROCm release

specialization.verdict: Balanced utilization and confident per-token routing are measured. Distinct routing by data source is weak: between-source JS is 0.9 to 2.3 percent of the divergence ceiling. Learned expert specialization is not supported: expert outputs became more similar and the expert residual ratio fell, while weight-space cross-expert cosine stayed near zero.
